brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base structure is present (portable organizer body).
requirements.evidence: Three full hex base pieces at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0), locked with two joint bolts; check_build shows no LOOSE_BODY, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Removable bins for small parts: at least two bins.
requirements.evidence: Two hex-bin-full bins (role R2) seated in cells (0,0) and (1,0); they drop in and hang on their rim.

A drawer-frame notch (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm, family notch) sits at (0,1) beside the two bases. No family 'drawer' part was offered: drawers need a half base's cut face, and this build uses full bases only. So the build has a drawer frame, not a drawer part, and no drawer is fitted inside it.
Top cover at (-1,0) (cover family) carries a handle (handle:-1,0,0;top) with inserts; this is the carry handle.

requirements.requirement: Portability: the build stays a compact single assembly under about 40 parts.
requirements.evidence: About 13 parts (3 bases, 2 bins, 1 drawer-frame notch, 1 cover, 1 handle with inserts, 2 joint bolts); meshClash clear, one connected assembly.

finish.summary: Built a compact three-base organizer with two removable bins, a carry handle on a top cover, and joint bolts locking the bases. The drawer requirement is only partly met: the only drawer-type option offered was a drawer-frame notch beside the bases, not a drawer part, and I did not find a way to get a true drawer on full bases. The checks are clean (meshClash clear, no loose body). Material and portability-in-use (weight, durability) are not checked here.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
